# Ancestry-Aware GWAS Workflow Boundary

## Use When

Use this workflow for an admixed or multi-ancestry cohort when global structure,
local ancestry, or ancestry-specific effects are part of the question.

## Stages

1. Lock the reference build, sample manifest, phenotype definition, and QC plan.
2. Perform genotype QC and relatedness assessment.
3. Estimate global structure and decide whether a conventional mixed-model GWAS
   answers the question.
4. For local ancestry, phase the cohort and infer ancestry using versioned
   reference panels and an external validated method such as RFMix.
5. Run the selected test: standard SNP GWAS with PCs/kinship, admixture mapping,
   or ancestry-specific association using an external tool such as Tractor.
6. Validate calibration, sensitivity to reference panels/covariates, and, for
   simulations, local-ancestry and causal-effect recovery.

## Package Boundary

The current package may create a structured synthetic benchmark and run its
ordinary mixed-model GWAS. It does not automatically phase cohorts, infer local
ancestry, or execute Tractor. That boundary should be shown clearly in agent
answers and reports.
